text:
The same Kyoto food hall stocks different sweets on different days. Thursday brings freshly pounded mochi, Saturday brings ohagi, and one dorayaki at Daimaru appears only three days a month 👇

👀 One of these surprised even us (the dates are here) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-depachika-gifts

📅 KYOTO'S SWEET CALENDAR (JR Kyoto Isetan B1, November 2026 list)

🍡 Thursday: Nakamuraken's mugite-mochi, freshly pounded rice cake with kinako to sprinkle on, from 11:00 (3 for ¥1,053). Mitamaya's black-syrup dango start too.

🍡 Saturday: Imanishiken's ohagi from 11:00, three for ¥721.

🍡 Sunday: mugite-mochi again, from 10:00.

🍡 Almost every day: Fuka's fu-manju wrapped in a bamboo leaf.

🌙 And at Daimaru Kyoto: Sasaya Iori's dorayaki is sold only on the 20th to 22nd of each month, around Toji's monthly Kobo-san market.

⚠️ THE MISTAKE TO AVOID

Buying fresh mochi as a gift for home. These are made to eat today. For the suitcase, pick baked yatsuhashi or a yokan instead.

The store also says arrival days can change and some items sell out, so treat this as a plan, not a promise.
